newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares surge ahead, correction expected.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares surge ahead, correction expected.

text.p: Zimbabwe's stock market continued bullish on Tuesday but brokers predicted the main industrial index, which crossed the 10,000 barrier on Monday, would start coming off soon on price corrections.
"I don't see it surging ahead much longer. It might actually start coming off soon," one broker said.
But on Tuesday the 57-counter index continued to surge ahead adding 91.30 points to close at 10,097.50.

The day's advancers include bankers FMB, which lept 480 cents to 5,000 and cement producer Porthold, clothing retailer Edgars and Barclays, another banker, which all added 100 cents to 1,575, 4,600 and 3350 respectively.

Other counters to gain were farming implement manufacturers Zimplow, which put on 90 cents to 700, tyre company NTS which went up 50 cents to 600, wire and cable makers Bicaf, 35 cents firmer at 580 and financial group udc and door and window manufacturer Radar, which both added 20 cents to 350 and 450 respectively.
Wine-maker Cairns went up 25 cents to 1,425 and electronics firm Apex and tyre group Dunlop finished off the winners list, adding 15 cents to 265 and 200 respectively.

The losers included retailers Tedco, which shed 60 cents to 1,140, Zimbabwe Alloys which lost 25 cents to 750, tobacco firm TSL 30 cents down at 750 and building material seller J and F, which was 5 cents easier at 240.

Minings were a bit stronger on the back of firmer international gold prices over the last few days. Gold producers Falcon went up 175 cents to 1,200 while Ashanti surged 1,000 cents to 10,000. The seven-counter index there added 1.24 points to 1,148.40.
